'''Saul Arno Teukolsky''' (born August 2, 1947, [[Johannesburg, South Africa]]) is a theoretical [[astrophysicist]] and a professor of [[Physics]] and [[Astronomy]] at [[Caltech]] and [[Cornell University]]. His major research interests include general relativity, relativistic astrophysics, and computational astrophysics.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Saul Teukolsky {{!}} Department of Astronomy |url=https://astro.cornell.edu/saul-teukolsky |access-date=2024-05-20 |website=astro.cornell.edu}}</ref>

==Biography==
{{BLP sources section|date=February 2024}}
After matriculating from [[Selborne College]] (East London, South Africa) in 1964, Teukolsky received a [[Bachelor of Science#Australia, New Zealand, and South Africa|Bachelor of Science in Honors]] Physics and Honors Applied Mathematics from the [[University of the Witwatersrand]], [[South Africa]] in 1970. He went on to be a graduate student under [[Kip Thorne]] at [[Caltech]] where he received his [[Ph.D.]] in 1973.

He joined [[Cornell University]] as an Assistant Professor of Physics and Astronomy in 1974 after serving as the Richard Chace Tolman Research Fellow for one year at [[Caltech]]. He was promoted to Associate Professor in 1977 and Full Professor in 1983.  In 1999 he was named the [[Hans A. Bethe]] professor of physics and astrophysics, a position which he still holds. In 2017 he was also appointed as Robinson Professor of Theoretical Astrophysics at [[Caltech]].

Teukolsky is one of the pioneers of [[numerical relativity]]: the subject that deals with equations involving [[general relativity]] using supercomputers. He is a coauthor of the [[Numerical Recipes]] series of books on scientific computing.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Numerical Recipes |url=http://www.numerical.recipes/ |access-date=2026-08-24 |website=www.numerical.recipes}}</ref> Today his research group works on numerical relativity calculations to predict signals from the [[LIGO]] and [[Laser Interferometer Space Antenna|LISA]] experiments.<ref>{{Cite web |title=LIGO Lab {{!}} Caltech {{!}} MIT |url=https://www.ligo.caltech.edu/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260823020812/https://www.ligo.caltech.edu/ |archive-date=2026-08-23 |access-date=2026-08-24 |website=LIGO Lab {{!}} Caltech}}</ref>

==Awards==

* Alfred P. Sloan Fellow, 1973
* John Simon Guggenheim Fellow, 1981
* Forefronts of Large-Scale Computing Award, 1990
* Fellow of the American Physical Society, 1994
* Fellow of the American Astronomical Society.
* Member of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences, 1996
* Member of the National Academy of Sciences, 2003
* [[Dirac Medal (ICTP)|Dirac Medal]] of the ICTP,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dirac Medallists 2021 {{!}} ICTP |url=https://www.ictp.it/home/dirac-medallists-2021 |access-date=2026-08-24 |website=www.ictp.it}}</ref> 2021
* [[Einstein Prize (APS)|Einstein prize]] of APS (joint with [[Clifford Martin Will|Clifford Will]]), 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|title=2021 Einstein Prize Recipients: Clifford Will & Saul Teukolsky|url=https://www.springer.com/gp/livingreviews/relativity/news/2021-einstein-prize-recipients-clifford-will-saul-teukolsky/18457834|access-date=2022-01-03|website=www.springer.com|language=en}}</ref>
